vignette: Akua had always been proud to serve her community as a police officer. But everything changed on the night she was assaulted by a fellow cop. The pain and humiliation still lingered, etched in her mind like an open wound. When memories of that night flooded back, she felt physical pain in the same parts of her body where she had been hurt - it was as if the trauma was still happening. The rage that accompanied these recollections left her breathless and shaking. In the aftermath, Akua couldn't shake the feeling that she was somehow to blame for what happened. She would often think about how life would have been different if only she had reacted faster or more assertively - counterfactual thoughts that tormented her with the possibilities of a different outcome. She started to believe that someone else in her shoes wouldn't have ended up in this situation, and that this was proof of some fundamental flaw within herself. As these self-doubts intensified, Akua began to withdraw from the very community she had once felt so connected to. Her husband noticed the change in her first - how she would snap at him for no reason, or become distant during conversations. She couldn't explain why she was acting this way, only that the world seemed darker and more menacing than before. Even simple tasks like going to the grocery store or meeting friends became daunting challenges, as if every social interaction held a hidden threat. Akua's memories of the assault were fragmented - there were parts she simply couldn't recall no matter how hard she tried. This lack of clarity only added to her feelings of guilt and inadequacy. She would find herself wondering what had really happened during those lost moments, whether there was something more she could have done to prevent it all. Her colleagues at the police department noticed a change in her too - Akua used to be known for her fearlessness on patrol, but now she would hesitate before responding to certain calls. She avoided confrontations whenever possible and started taking fewer risks, as if trying to prove to herself that she was still capable of doing her job. Akua's self-comparison to others had become a constant refrain in her mind - the feeling that someone else wouldn't have ended up like this haunted her every step of the way. Her husband tried to reassure her that it wasn't her fault, but Akua couldn't shake off the conviction that she was somehow broken beyond repair. The memories still lingered, triggering rage and pain that left her gasping for breath. To cope, Akua continued to withdraw from the world around her - avoiding emotional stress became an all-consuming goal. Situations that might make her feel strong emotions were studiously avoided, as if any display of vulnerability would be catastrophic. In recent weeks, however, the isolation had started to suffocate her. The realization dawned on her that she couldn't keep living like this - in constant fear of her own memories and trapped by the shame that followed. That's when Akua finally made up her mind to seek help - a tentative first step towards reclaiming the life she once knew, before the assault stole it away from her. As she sat in the therapist's office for their first session, Akua couldn't help but wonder what would happen if she actually allowed herself to confront these memories head-on. Would she be able to find some semblance of peace and reconnection with her community? Or was that part of her lost forever, trapped behind a wall of pain and self-doubt?
